item.title: 49ers executive John Lynch has alarming comment about rampant fighting with Raiders fans
item.description: President of football operations and general manager John Lynch curiously addressed the fan brawls after the San Francisco 49ers' 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
item.content:encoded:
John Lynch was talking about the San Francisco 49ers' win, right?

Lynch, the team's president of football operations and general manager, addressed the brawls that took place in the parking lot and inside Levi's Stadium during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I was kind of pleased this is going pretty well throughout the game and then the fourth quarter broke out," Lynch said, according to the New York Post.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"You see videos after … it’s a shame but it kind of goes with the territory. It’s a shame to see those things, but it was a good hard-fought win for us. There was a lot of silver and black in the stadium that’s for sure."

The fighting was rampant throughout the game, as 45 people were ejected and nearly a dozen were arrested, Santa Clara police told SFGATE. Seven of the 11 people were arrested for disorderly conduct, while the other four were arrested for allegedly fighting in a public place.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Incidents of violence at large-scale events in Santa Clara will not be tolerated," Santa Clara Police Department spokesperson Lt. Eric Lagergren told the outlet. "The Department strictly enforces the law and holds individuals accountable for criminal conduct. We will seek to arrest the individuals responsible for the fan-on-fan violence at the event."

The Battle of the Bay may not be as heated as it once was, but it's clear there is no love lost based on what happened Sunday. While Lynch was likely talking about the 49ers' win rather than the fans' performance in the parking lot brawl, it was still an eyebrow-raising comment.

item.title: Protecting failing schools and supporting teachers unions is not a winnable strategy, CEO warns
item.description: Tommy Schultz of the American Federation for Children says Democrats' reliance on teachers unions and opposition to school choice is a losing strategy.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats’ reliance on teachers union support and allegiance to underperforming public school systems is a losing political strategy, according to Tommy Schultz, CEO of the conservative advocacy group American Federation for Children (AFC).

"At the end of the day, when you look at the long-term trends here for the teachers unions, they're in a pickle because more and more folks are listening to the politicians that have a vibrant education agenda," Schultz told Fox News Digital.

"And they aren't just saying, 'We want to block all possible options,' because the unions really don't have an agenda other than, 'We want to keep your kids forced to go to the schools that we run and control,'" Schultz added. "It's not a winning message at the end of the day."

MEMBER OF LARGEST TEACHERS UNION IN US CLAIMS ORG IS 'NO LONGER FOCUSED ON CHILDREN,' ONLY 'POLITICAL POWER'

Teachers unions consistently oppose many school choice initiatives supported by advocacy organizations like the AFC. They argue that programs such as vouchers and education savings accounts siphon taxpayer funds away from public schools. Union leaders maintain those dollars should instead be directed toward boosting teacher salaries, recruiting staff, and upgrading public school facilities.

Democratic candidates in gubernatorial, congressional, and state legislative races routinely back education platforms aligned with teachers unions. Financial analyses indicate the nation's two largest teachers unions — the National Education Association (NEA) and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) — have spent hundreds of millions of dollars into political activism, lobbying, and progressive advocacy over the past decade.

While the NEA and AFT rank among the largest financial contributors to Democratic campaigns, both organizations have occasionally supported select Republican candidates in rural districts who advocated for state aid for underfunded public schools.

Tensions between unions and parents have intensified in recent years, fueled by concerns over learning loss following pandemic-era school closures. In response, Republicans have campaigned heavily on school choice, enacting measures to provide families with state-funded vouchers and education savings accounts to access private or alternative educational settings outside their assigned neighborhood districts.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

However, recent Democratic wins in key state races could create headwinds for the school choice movement. In Texas, Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has signaled opposition to the state's school voucher program after defeating Republican Gov. Greg Abbott in the November 3 election. Hinojosa's victory raises questions about the future of Abbott's signature school choice legislation, which established one of the nation's largest education savings account programs.

"Fundamentally, I think it's a knee-jerk reaction to the largest funders of the Democratic Party," Schultz told Fox News Digital. "The teachers unions, they bring in about $3 billion a year for the teachers unions — the two national unions and their affiliates, so, they're a real big driver of the primary politics and Democratic politics in particular."

The Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) program, created by the state legislature with an initial $1 billion allocation, expanded access to private-school tuition and other approved education expenses for eligible families. The program allows parents to direct state funds toward alternative education options, raising questions about the potential financial impact on traditional public school districts.

Major urban school districts across the country have faced steep enrollment declines since the COVID-19 pandemic. Some large districts, including Houston Independent School District (HISD), have faced challenges retaining students amid changing enrollment patterns and competition from other education options.

DENVER MOTHER FIGHTS FOR HER DAUGHTER'S EDUCATION AS ADVOCATES MAKE NATIONWIDE SCHOOL CHOICE PUSH

Despite legislative hurdles in some states, Schultz expressed confidence that parental demand for school choice will continue to drive political outcomes.

"What we found over the last chunk of years is that when you actually bring a message of pro-school choice policies and a brighter vision of education — of what could happen to public schools and for families controlling their child's educational destiny — those candidates win," Schultz said.

The AFT and Hinojosa did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

The NEA provided Fox News Digital with a statement it released following the November 3 midterm elections.

"Across the nation, most Americans want the same thing — a more affordable future, strong public schools and safer communities. And they’re ready to slam the door on corruption and self-dealing," National Education Association President Princess Moss said.

"Tonight, voters came together across race, place and gender and sent a clear message and mandate: put working families, students and educators first and deliver for our communities, not billionaires and corporations," she added.

item.title: Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart handed 3-game ban after swinging at Warriors center Charles Bassey
item.description: Marcus Smart faces a three-game NBA suspension after punching Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey in Houston's 115-108 win over Golden State.
item.content:encoded:
A late-game punch just cost Marcus Smart three games. The NBA suspended the Houston Rockets guard without pay on Thursday after swinging at, then grazing, Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey.

Doing the exact opposite of his last name, the 32-year-old former Defensive Player of the Year melted down in the third quarter of Houston's 115-108 win.

Smart and Bassey got tied up fighting for position under the glass, barked at each other trailing the play, and Smart uncorked a right hook that grazed Bassey's nose. Teammates, coaches, and officials quickly stepped between them.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Smart did not wait for the replay review to finish before walking toward the locker room. Referees assessed him a Flagrant 2 foul and the 13th ejection of his career, ending his night with six points, two rebounds, and one assist in 17 minutes. He will sit out Friday's home matchup against the Utah Jazz, Sunday's road game in Washington and Monday's trip to Miami before becoming eligible to return Nov. 18 against the Indiana Pacers.

After the game, Rockets head coach Ime Udoka relayed Smart's excuse for throwing hands.

FAN EJECTED FROM NBA GAME AFTER HITTING FEMALE REF WITH BALL AS MELODRAMATIC LAKERS STAR THROWS TANTRUM

According to Udoka, Smart claimed Bassey wrapped up Smart's previously injured elbow during the tangle.

When Smart confronted him about it, Bassey allegedly replied, "What you gonna do?"

"And he did it," Udoka told reporters.

Bassey, who finished with seven points and six rebounds in 13 minutes, was unimpressed by the swing and unloaded on Smart in the locker room.

Bassey accused Smart of playing dirty all night, alleging the guard grabbed his knee while Bassey tried to set a screen in the first half. Bassey admitted he baited Smart into reacting and dismissed the punch as an excuse to clock out early.

"I knew he was gonna do something," he said. "I baited for him to do something, because I knew he was going to do something. I don't think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game. He wasn't trying to play … I think he was trying to chill. He wasn't trying to hoop, bro."

The ban marks the third NBA suspension of Smart's 13-year career, following one-game league bans for hitting Matt Bonner in 2015 and threatening an official in 2021, plus more than a dozen fines that include a $50,000 penalty for shoving Joel Embiid in 2019.

Houston still closed out the seven-point win, but Smart's thin skin will cost him three games and six figures.

item.title: Super Bowl champion Kyle Van Noy details what really happens when a player gets traded at the deadline
item.description: Super Bowl champion Kyle Van Noy revealed the behind-the-scenes chaos of his 2016 trade from the Detroit Lions to the New England Patriots.
item.content:encoded:
Ever wonder what it’s like to be traded in the NFL midseason? Well, if you have, you are in luck.

Super Bowl champion Kyle Van Noy, who currently plays for the Minnesota Vikings, took to social media to share his experience of being traded at the deadline. The 35-year-old was traded from the Detroit Lions to the New England Patriots in 2016.

"I got a call from the Lions GM at the time saying I was traded (he forgot to tell me until the end of the call where I was traded to). You then get a call from the team that traded for you (patriots). They set a flight up with you as fast as possible," Van Noy said on X.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

He explained that the team that acquires a player wants to bring him in as fast as possible to complete a physical. Van Noy said teams want to avoid a situation like the one involving Maxx Crosby during the offseason, when the Baltimore Ravens backed out of a trade days after agreeing to it with the Las Vegas Raiders because of concerns about his physical.

Van Noy said teams will help players with some moving and living arrangements after a trade.

"The only thing when I was traded the team took care of was moving. Teams give you a certain amount of money for movers and shipping your car. Lastly, team takes care of about 10 days or 2 weeks paid for a hotel room until you can find your own living," Van Noy said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

However, when it comes to a player's previous residence, they are responsible for handling those arrangements themselves.

"You can sell the house with a realtor if you bought one in the city you play in or renting you gotta pay the rest of the rent even if you are not living in it," Van Noy said.

Van Noy hasn't been traded midseason since 2016 and said things could have changed since then, but he believes the process remains largely the same.

Van Noy is in his 13th NFL season and his first with the Vikings. He has played for six different teams during his career. He spent the first two and a half seasons of his career with the Lions before being traded to the Patriots, where he spent three and a half seasons.

He was with the Miami Dolphins for one season before returning to the Patriots. Van Noy then signed with the Los Angeles Chargers, where he spent one season before playing the following three seasons with the Baltimore Ravens.

In his first season with the Vikings, he has recorded 15 total tackles and 1.5 sacks in eight games.

item.title: Former F1 grid girl wants Sydney Sweeney to bring the models back to the track ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix
item.description: Leilani Dowding wants Sydney Sweeney as a grid girl at the Las Vegas GP, saying the actress would make critics rage with steam out of their heads.
item.content:encoded:
English model and former F1 grid girl Leilani Dowding has long been a supporter of bringing the models back to the Formula 1 racetrack. They were removed from the sport prior to the 2018 season in a move she's never understood.

It was argued at the time that the models no longer aligned with its brand values. The 46-year-old model disagreed with the decision then and she still does. She was in Los Angeles when the news broke and found out about it in the papers.

"I thought it was crazy. I remember thinking, 'what is going on?' It was always really welcoming," she told GrandPrix247 in a recent interview.

"The only people who would say stupid things, such as that we were being objectified, were people who weren't involved and had never spoken to us. They were looking in from the outside."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Dowding thinks the time for grid girls to return to Formula 1 is now. The modern, more entertainment-focused approach, especially at next week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, would be a natural fit.

She has an A-list actress in mind to lead the way and bring the grid girls back to Formula 1. The one and only Sydney Sweeney.

STEAMY SYDNEY SWEENEY AD DRAWS BACKLASH FROM FEMALE ATHLETES

"Sydney Sweeney would make a fantastic grid girl. I'd love to see her doing it for the Las Vegas GP, she'd be one of my favorites. She should get her boots on and get on that grid," Dowding said.

"I think she'd be wonderful. She'd make so many people angry, especially because you can just imagine them raging, with steam coming out of their heads."

Leilani Dowding doesn’t just want to see grid girls back in F1. She wants to take what the sport is already doing with celebrities and entertainment before the green flag and put it on steroids while ruffling a few feathers.

Who better to accomplish all of that than Sydney Sweeney? Not only can she pull it all off, she won't be phased by any of the haters.

I don’t think we'll see the actress leading grid girls back out to the track in Las Vegas next week, but maybe we will one day.

Dowding has a solid "Make F1 Great Again" plan if you ask me. All that's needed is for someone to implement it.

item.title: Ex-NBA player Gilbert Arenas responds to Steph Curry, stands by calling wife Ayesha a family 'blemish'
item.description: Gilbert Arenas offered a conditional apology on his podcast after Steph Curry posted a video defending Ayesha Curry against critical comments.
item.content:encoded:
Former Golden State Warriors player Gilbert Arenas clarified his comments about current Warriors star Stephen Curry’s wife, Ayesha, but stopped short of offering a full apology.

Speaking on his "Gil’s Arena" podcast, Arenas said his comments were intended to point out that Steph typically avoids controversy while identifying what he called a "blemish" on the Curry family.

"All I said is he doesn’t get in trouble for nothing," Arenas said. "He says the right things. If you gotta judge this family, his only blemish is what his wife said. That’s all I said. If there is a blemish, it’s that." The three-time All-Star later expressed regret if his comments offended Steph, but maintained that he had not intended them as a personal attack.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I’m sorry if he’s offended. I didn’t mean it like that. I was just saying that he’s such a perfect dude… but I am sorry."

Nick Young, who is a "Gil's Arena" contributor, provided a more direct apology. "This man Gil won’t say sorry at all. I’m sorry, Steph. You my dog. I love you. If I offended you, I apologize like a man. I’m sorry," Young said. Young was Curry’s teammate for one season in Golden State, winning the 2018 NBA title with the Warriors.

Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho also apologized to the Currys for comments he made on a separate podcast.

AYESHA CURRY SAYS HUSBAND STEPH CURRY'S NBA PREGAME HABITS INSPIRED HER MOVIE CHARACTER, RESPONDS TO BACKLASH

"When a man humbly comes to you and requests an apology, then you wouldn’t be ignorant to respond with anything else than I’m sorry," Acho said. "Steph, I’m sorry for not just offending you but potentially offending your wife. I’m sorry for how it may have made you feel."

Acho added: "I’m sorry for how it may have made you feel seeing headlines, commentary, all these things about your wife," Acho said, referring to the reaction to Ayesha’s starring role in the Roku romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday."

"I’m sorry for the reactions it may have caused internally, vicariously among you, in your central and nervous system."

The string of mea culpas came to light shortly after Curry took to social media to address criticism of his wife of 15 years.

"Usually the noise doesn’t bother me, it doesn’t bother Ayesha, but this one in particular, when you’re trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife and, you know, obviously needing podcasts, tapings and topics and giving opinions on somebody else’s wife," Curry said in an Instagram video posted on Wednesday.

STEPHEN CURRY ISSUES RARE PUBLIC RESPONSE TO CRITICS, DEFENDS WIFE AYESHA AMID ACTING-ROLE BACKLASH

One scene in the film calls for Ayesha to kiss co-star Matthew Daddario, a moment that sparked debate and criticism among sports figures on social media.

"Nick, Gil, Emmanuel, and anybody else who feels the need to wanna have to, you know, jump in and give an opinion of something you don’t really know about, something that kinda speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they’re allowed and what they’re not allowed to do."

After defending his wife, Curry closed with a pointed thank you to the critics for the unsolicited publicity.

On the basketball front, Curry is expected to miss at least two weeks due to an oblique abdominal tear. ESPN reported Thursday, citing sources, that the Warriors are anticipating the star guard will be sidelined for closer to a month.

Curry’s night ended early Wednesday when he left the Warriors’ game against the Houston Rockets with less than seven minutes remaining in the first quarter. He later underwent an MRI. Houston won 115-108.

item.title: Here's how bad the College Football Playoff's selection committee rankings actually are | Ian Miller
item.description: College Football Playoff poll has Miami Hurricanes ranked five spots too low and Boise State nine spots below where efficiency metrics place them.
item.content:encoded:
It's been two weeks of the College Football Playoff poll and two weeks of seemingly unending controversy.

What the selection committee values, playing in one conference, and what fans and other analysts value, seems to be two very different things. There are any number of rankings that are controversial, confusing, or downright inexplicable. And committee chair Hunter Yurachek's attempted explanations during the post-release interview have only served to make things worse, rather than provide clarification for their thinking.

But it's easy to complain, subjectively, saying that one ranking or another doesn't make sense or isn't consistent with prior thinking. What though, would be the best system for putting teams in order? Or at least, a significantly better one that doesn't overly rely on the often-misleading "eye test" and inherent biases from committee members.

NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF POLL PROVES THE SELECTION COMMITTEE IS JUST MAKING IT UP AS THEY GO

Fortunately, some outside analysts have come up with their own way of comparing a more objective set of rankings to the committee's uh, heavily influenced poll.

ESPN's Bill Connelly created a blended set of metrics to better evaluate important performance metrics. Essentially using an 80/20 combination, with the 80 side being resume rankings, strength of record, the "football power index," and the 20 side being forward-looking ratings.

WE NEED TO ABOLISH THE CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE AFTER YET ANOTHER EMBARRASSMENT

These are opponent adjusted, and focus more heavily on underlying efficiency on offense, defense and special teams. That's a better methodology for predicting how teams perform moving forward, considering wins and losses are noisy and often influenced by fluky outcomes.

So how does it look?

Well, you'll be stunned to hear that, once again, a specific conference has received a tremendous benefit of the doubt that they do not deserve, and that the Miami Hurricanes can feel especially aggrieved with the treatment they received after taking their first loss. Here's the list, with the arrows representing the position these teams are in Connelly's rankings, relative to the playoff poll. For example, Miami at No. 2 in Connelly's list is five spots higher than they are in the actual rankings.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Pretty impressive for there to be just one spot that matches! This is just one set of rankings, not necessarily definitive, and others have different outcomes, but it's an indication of how the committee values things that they shouldn't, while ignoring things they should care about.

Unsurprisingly, Kentucky is the biggest "miss" by the committee, as the Wildcats are still getting an immense amount of credit for their "SEC" schedule, ignoring that their performances don't warrant it. South Carolina is eight spots too high in the committee poll, again, given a tremendous amount of deference to simply existing in the SEC.

On the other hand, Boise State is nine spots too low, because the committee is incapable of appreciating performances against teams that do not play in the SEC.

Indiana and Wake Forest are underrated, Alabama is overrated, surprise, surprise, and Miami's six spot drop after losing to Notre Dame looks even more absurd. What might be a surprise though, and what would create some controversy, is the rankings for Ohio State and LSU.

The Buckeyes and Tigers both now have three losses, but computer-driven metrics give them credit for how they've played, while being unaware of Julian Sayin's injury. Efficiency-driven systems are much slower to react to losses to good teams than humans are, and the Buckeyes' three losses have been to Texas, USC and Oregon, while their win over Indiana and dominance against other opponents like Iowa still pushes them into the top-15.

Similarly, LSU gets credit for playing well in losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky, putting them higher than the committee's ranking.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Overall though, there are nine SEC teams in the CFB playoff top-25 poll. Seven of them are higher than they'd be using an objective metric. Missouri sits at No. 28 in Connelly's rankings, and No. 22 in the poll. Just because. On average, even including LSU at -8 spots, the average miss per SEC team was 2.5 spots higher than their performance-based ranking.

That is the problem; the SEC has spent years building itself up through concerted marketing efforts, the people that run the sport believe them, for some reason, and then teams are rated based on inaccurate assumptions. That's bad! There are tens of millions of dollars and jobs at stake, and the committee's obsession with rewarding SEC mediocrity is jeopardizing all of it. And the very legitimacy of the process.

The worst part? If, by some miracle, the committee corrected for this bias moving forward, the SEC fans, boosters and commissioner Greg Sankey would be livid. Beyond livid. The complaining, whining, anger and press conferences would be relentless. Until they got their way again anyway.

Once you get used to privilege, it's hard to give it up.

item.title: Gal Gadot cheers new Skydance co-CEO for 'sticking up against antisemitism'
item.description: Gal Gadot nearly broke into tears presenting Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz with the Simon Wiesenthal Center's Humanitarian Award for his stance against antisemitism.
item.content:encoded:
Israeli actress and former "Wonder Woman" star Gal Gadot nearly broke into tears while praising Skydance's new co-CEO, Ynon Kreiz, for "sticking up against antisemitism" during the Simon Wiesenthal Center’s Humanitarian Award Dinner Wednesday.

Gadot joined movie producer Jeffrey Katzenberg and Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison in presenting Kreiz with the 2026 Humanitarian Award. While presenting the award, she expressed horror at the rise of bigotry against Jewish people since 2023.

"I’m frightened by how quickly hatred of Jews is spreading and how openly it is expressed and accepted," Gadot said, according to Variety. 

"Since the Oct. 7 massacre and the war that followed, I have found myself asking how far this can go. If people get used to hearing and seeing hatred and looking the other way, then where does it end?"

ISRAELI ACTRESS CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD STARS 'SILENCING ARTISTS' WHO SUPPORT JEWISH STATE

Gadot, who is Jewish, has long defended Israel after the deadly Oct. 7 Hamas attacks and praised Kreiz for his leadership amid the rise of antisemitism.

"What gives me hope is that people like Ynon aren’t wavering," she continued. "He’s doing what he’s always done. He’s standing firm. He feels what our community is going through. 

"He’s sticking up against antisemitism. He’s bringing his intense conviction and heart to this fight. He’s leading. That leadership is like a beacon of light and, in a dark hour, nothing matters more than a ray of light to give all of us courage."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Simon Wiesenthal Center and Skydance for comment.

MICHAEL RAPAPORT TELLS CRAIG CARTON THAT HIS SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL HAS COST HIM WORK IN HOLLYWOOD

After accepting the award, Kreiz, who is an Israeli, British and American citizen, thanked Ellison and Skydance for taking a "bold stand for Israel and the Jewish people" against what he called an "ancient hatred."

"We recognize that business leadership comes with moral responsibility," Kreiz said, according to Deadline.

Kreiz's award came just over one month after Paramount Skydance's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Before the merger closed, Ellison announced that Kreiz, who previously served as chairman and CEO of Mattel, would serve as co-CEO alongside him.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, the Israeli-American Council (IAC) congratulated Kreiz on the award and emphasized the need to speak up against antisemitism.

PARAMOUNT ACCUSES MARK RUFFALO OF INVOKING 'ANTISEMITIC TROPES' IN WARNER BROS DISCOVERY MERGER DISPUTE

"Gal Gadot is right to speak about the concerns around the spread of hatred of Jews," the IAC statement read. 

"No Jewish actor, writer, employee or student should have to wonder whether speaking about antisemitism or expressing support for Israel would cost them work, friendships or acceptance. 

"Opposing hatred of Jews should not require an act of professional courage. And when it does, something is deeply wrong."

item.title: Indie wrestling star Effy prepares for battle with Slade, fires warning to Dr Wagner Jr ahead of PRODUCE shows
item.description: Effy takes on Slade in a bloody bounty match in Kingston, New York, then battles Lucha Libre legend Dr. Wagner Jr. at Lucha Fresca in Brooklyn.
item.content:encoded:
Effy will be in the fights of his life this weekend as he has two matches on the docket as part of PRODUCE Wrestling’s back-to-back showcase in New York.

The 6-foot-2 superstar will face off against Slade in a bounty match in what will likely be a bloody affair for PRODUCE Wrestling’s Assembly event in Kingston on Saturday night. Then, in Brooklyn, Effy will take on Lucha Libre legend Dr. Wagner Jr. at Lucha Fresca.

Slade is someone who is going to bring the fight with him in every match he competes in and the two have wrestled before. He’s one of the toughest guys on the independent wrestling scene and isn’t someone to take lightly. But Effy knows that. The two have a long and storied history in which, according to Effy, led to Slade taking a hiatus from the ring for two years after one of their matches.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

He lamented having to take Slade off of his "chart" of pro wrestlers he’s faced and retired in an interview with OutKick Dropkick.

"I had to take it off my chart because there's been a list of people that have wrestled me and retired, and I don't think it's because the match was bad, I don't think it's because I ruined their thought of wrestling. I think they got in the ring, and there's a lot of perception about Effy, you know, you may have just learned a little bit about me, but there's 10 years of Effy you can go find where I've wrestled your Jeff Jarretts, I've wrestled your JBLs, I've wrestled your (Jon) Moxleys, I've wrestled your Jinder Mahals, all your favorites have come, through Effy and it's all there and, to now sort stand in this position where I can make or break a guy's life ‘cause they look in my eyes and they decide, ‘I don't know if I'm all the way committed to pro wrestling the way Effy is, I don't know if I'm ready to live this s--- all the time.’ I have people come talk to me and they go, ‘This isn't a character, you're Effy, you're committed to pro wrestling, you're in this.’

"Slade came back, and so I had to take him off my list to fight Slade again. And knowing what Slade puts up on the table … Here’s the thing I learned, you can talk to Slade all you want, he's gonna do whatever he wants. It's crazy. But now, I have history with Slade. I've been in there with Slade, I've felt him when he has the advantage of numbers, and now, if it's just me and him, I've got things to get out of my system, and for him to return to wrestling and for him to knowingly know, the last time or one of the times he wrestled me, he disappeared from this business for two years, they can say what they want about, ‘Oh, is Effy scared of Slade?’ But historically, I have made or break careers along the way."

Effy made clear there was no way he was going to miss Lucha Fresca in Brooklyn.

He detailed the list of historic Lucha Libre wrestlers he’s already put away in his career, including Pimpanella Escarletta and Psycho Clown. He was very much looking forward to beating Dr. Wagner Jr., especially in front of the legend’s sons.

"I thought he would have left after we found out he was a hot silver daddy when he unmasked and everybody could see him. I thought he would have gone into telenovelas, I thought he would've left wrestling, I thought he would've gotten the f--- out of taking bumps, but it's because of his stupid hot sons that he now wants to do more. We got El Hijo del Dr Wagner Jr., who is so hot. I got to see him in Tokyo, and I'm like, Jesus, this is before I've ever met Dr. Wagner. And then Galeno Del Mal, who is, I didn't realize how much I was into bears until I saw Galeno Del Mal, and he is just a thick muscle daddy, and so now you're letting me fight your dad?

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I am going to make these boys think about things they have never thought about. I'm gonna make Dr. Wagner Jr. understand that Effy is a real-life Lucha Libre legend, whether anyone wants to admit it or not, and I will put him into a situation where he's going to have to decide how hard he's willing to get hit to get through Effy, and his boys are gonna watch me beat his dad up, and they're gonna come over and they're gonna have realizations about their life, and I'm gonna say, ‘No. Effy’s busy, you need to stay with your wives, you need to stay with them and stay away from Effy, ‘cause I'm only bad news, but I beat up your dad and I want you to know I would dominate you. I would dominate you in a way where I would make you my housewife and it would be beautiful, but I want you to see what I'm doing to your dad here and that I still give him mercy, because he is a legend, and I'm honored to be in the ring with him, but I want those hot sons to see what I'm gonna do to Dr. Wagner Jr. … Entering this match, maybe there's a little underestimation, but I think deep in his heart, Dr. Wagner Jr. knows the reputation of Effy, that if he doesn't put up the fight of a lifetime, I'm gonna embarrass him in front of his boys and his boys are gonna wanna sit on my lap."

item.title: TSA discovers suspected cocaine worth $27,750 hidden in coffee container at airport
item.description: TSA officers at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport flagged a white substance hidden in a coffee container during a secondary baggage screening.
item.content:encoded:
What looked like a routine morning brew turned into a major drug bust at an Alaska airport recently.

Authorities discovered nearly $28,000 worth of suspected cocaine stashed inside a coffee container in a man's luggage on Nov. 11.

The discovery was made at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport after Transportation Security Administration (TSA) officers noticed what appeared to be a white, chalky substance during a secondary baggage screening, according to the Alaska Department of Public Safety.

BIZARRE X-RAY SCAN LEADS TSA OFFICERS TO FLIGHT PASSENGER'S ILLEGAL STASH

Investigators with the Anchorage Airport Interdiction Team responded at about 6:55 a.m. and determined the bag belonged to a 58-year-old resident of Selawik, Alaska, authorities said.

The substance had a gross weight of about 185 grams, or less than half a pound, and field-tested positive for cocaine, according to the department.

Authorities estimated the drugs would have a street value of $27,750 in the northwestern Alaska communities of Kotzebue and Selawik.

The man, Walter Berry, was contacted at the departure gate as he prepared to board a flight from Anchorage to Kotzebue, officials said. 

His final destination was Selawik, according to the department.

Investigators said Berry had possession of the luggage before it was checked for the flight.

He was arrested and taken to the Anchorage Correctional Complex on a charge of third-degree misconduct involving a controlled substance, authorities said.

The investigation remains ongoing with assistance from the Western Alaska Alcohol and Narcotics Team.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport and the Alaska Department of Public Safety for comment.

The discovery comes after a number of other unusual items have been flagged recently during airport security screenings.

Fox News Digital previously reported that TSA officers at New York's Watertown International Airport spotted something suspicious on an X-ray that turned out to be a spent M18 smoke grenade hidden inside an aerosol container in a passenger's carry-on bag.

The passenger reportedly told officers he'd forgotten the grenade was in his bag. An explosives expert later confirmed that it was not live.

In another incident at Tampa International Airport, a TSA officer noticed something unusual about a baseball bat-shaped flashlight while screening a passenger's carry-on bag.

A closer inspection revealed a 4-inch, double-edged knife concealed inside the flashlight.

Keith Jeffries, a Florida-based vice president of K2 Security Screening Group and former federal security director for TSA at Los Angeles International Airport, previously told Fox News Digital that travelers should not attempt to sneak prohibited items through airport security.

item.title: USA soccer sends emotional letter to players about pulling out of U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid Iran war
item.description: U.S. Soccer's letter to U-17 players reveals the emotional toll behind the Qatar World Cup withdrawal, citing the Level 3 travel advisory for Qatar.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Soccer expressed its "shared disappointment" in a letter to players explaining its withdrawal from the upcoming U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid safety concerns surrounding the Iran war.

The letter, obtained by Fox News Digital, praised the players and coaches for their preparation while explaining why the federation was canceling both its pre-tournament camp and participation in the competition.

"We are writing to inform you of the difficult decision to cancel our World Cup pre-camp and our planned participation in the World Cup. We are extremely proud of the preparation by our players and coaches to represent the US in the World Cup," the letter said.

TEAM USA WITHDRAWS FROM FIFA U-17 WORLD CUP AMID STATE DEPARTMENT TRAVEL WARNING IN MIDDLE EAST

"Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances including the US State Department’s Level 3 Travel Advisory for Qatar and related directives for Embassy staff and families, we are no longer able to participate in the tournament. The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority."

The withdrawal became public Wednesday, eight days before the tournament’s scheduled Nov. 19 start.

The letter also instructed players to hold off on publicly discussing the decision until FIFA announced it, while telling them their clubs would receive official notification.

"We will communicate this officially to your clubs today as well. We ask that you refrain from sharing this information or commenting publicly until such time that it has been communicated publicly by FIFA," the letter said.

"Again, please accept our deepest appreciation for your commitment to US Soccer and our shared disappointment about these circumstances."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The State Department’s Oct. 23 advisory urges Americans to reconsider travel to Qatar because of the risk of armed conflict. U.S. government employees must obtain special authorization to travel there.

The advisory cites attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces against civilian airports and other infrastructure in neighboring Saudi Arabia, warning that the hostilities could spread rapidly beyond the immediate area.

It also identifies risks to civilian aviation from regional political and military tensions. Americans who travel to Qatar are urged to prepare to shelter in place and have an emergency departure plan that does not depend on U.S. government assistance.

Fox News Digital previously reported that an Iranian missile struck Qatar’s Al-Udeid Air Base in March. Qatari officials reported no injuries.

Fox News Digital also reported that nonemergency U.S. government employees and their families were ordered out of Saudi Arabia on Oct. 23 over safety concerns.

For the American players, the withdrawal ends a World Cup opportunity less than a week after head coach Alex Aldaz announced his 21-player roster Nov. 6.

The Americans were scheduled to open against Montenegro on Nov. 21, face Chile on Nov. 24 and finish Group J play against Algeria on Nov. 27.

The roster included Philadelphia Union forward Malik Jakupovic, who scored eight goals during qualifying, and players affiliated with European clubs including AC Milan, Ajax and PSV.

The United States earned its place in February, winning its qualifying group in St. Vincent and the Grenadines. The Americans beat the hosts 8-0 and St. Kitts and Nevis 10-0 before clinching qualification with a 1-1 draw against the Dominican Republic.

Nine members of that qualifying squad were included on the World Cup roster.

This year’s competition is the second under the tournament’s expanded annual, 48-team format and the second of five consecutive editions awarded to Qatar.

FIFA published the tournament’s official squad lists Wednesday, outlining plans for 104 matches and a final at Ahmad bin Ali Stadium.

item.title: Federal Title IX probe rocks Camas School District after trans runner controversy, superintendent pushes back
item.description: Camas High's cross-country controversy deepens as the Department of Education opens a Title IX investigation into the district's handling of complaints.
item.content:encoded:
Think the controversy surrounding the male Camas High cross-country runner who switched to the girls' team ended when the season did?

Not even close.

OutKick has learned that the U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights opened an investigation into Washington state's Camas School District today to determine whether it violated Title IX.

A CROSS COUNTRY RUNNER SWITCHED TO THE GIRLS TEAM MIDSEASON, PARENTS VOICE THEIR DISAPPROVAL AT MEET

As was first reported by 570-KVI, parents and members of the Camas High girls' cross-country team alleged last month that the male runner entered a hotel room occupied by three female runners and took an ice bath in their bathroom while the team was traveling for an invitational meet. There are also allegations that the athlete sexually harassed female teammates, raising concerns about their privacy and safety.

Parents also accused the district of mishandling their complaints of sexual harassment. They alleged that an independent investigator failed to take steps to protect the girls and instead questioned whether they were "transphobic" or "hate trans people."

This all comes on the heels of the Camas runner switching from the boys to the girls' team in the middle of the season, which ended Saturday in the state finals. The runner finished 76th in a JV meet in his first race as a boy, but won a varsity meet upon switching to the girls' team and prevented girls from advancing to the regional and state meets.

The runner's presence on the girls' team sparked three separate protests from female athletes — including about a dozen of his own teammates — who walked off the starting line after the gun sounded rather than compete against him. Elise Bierer of Battle Ground High ended her season by walking off the starting line at the district meet.

The consequences for Camas School District? They could be significant. According to the DOE, a Title IX violation can result in the loss of federal funding.

But Camas School District Superintendent John Anzalone isn't particularly worried.

'HEARTBROKEN' WASHINGTON STATE SUPERINTENDENT SAYS NO CONSEQUENCES FOR GIRLS WHO PROTESTED TRANSGENDER RUNNER

In an interview with OutKick on Thursday, Anzalone said he was confident the district had handled the controversy appropriately and didn't expect the federal investigation to uncover any violations.

"I don't think there are going to be any violations," said Anzalone, emphasizing that he trusts that his staff acted appropriately throughout this ordeal. "And if there were, and we made a misstep somewhere, we'll move forward and correct that."

This came after a back-and-forth regarding the ice baths, which Anzalone downplayed. Last month, Clark County Today quoted an anonymous Camas parent who said the following:

"[Biological male’s name redacted] entered a hotel room shared by three girls to take an ice bath,’’ the parent said. "The ice bath is a CHS tradition, but it is, of course, against school policy for boys to enter girls' rooms and vice versa. Presumably, he stripped down to his shorts and sports bra like the girls do among themselves for the ice bath.’’

Anzalone, however, said the ice bath incident was "highly blown out of proportion" and that district administrators never felt anything inappropriate had occurred. He explained that the ice baths were a team tradition that district leadership hadn't been aware of.

He also clarified that the male runner stayed in a separate hotel room with his mother, rather than sharing one with female teammates.

I pushed back on Anzalone's characterization of the ice bath incident, pointing out that the tradition generally involves athletes of the same sex and that one girl reportedly felt uncomfortable enough to leave the room.

Anzalone said his understanding was that the girl left as soon as the transgender runner entered. He also reiterated that the district couldn't prevent an activity it didn't know was happening.

PARENTS SPEAK OUT ON THE INGRAHAM ANGLE AFTER GIRLS FORFEIT RACE OVER BIOLOGICAL MALE RUNNER

But when I asked whether he understood why mixing genders in such a setting would concern parents and athletes, he acknowledged the point.

"Yeah, absolutely, absolutely," Anzalone said. "I'm not denying that."

He maintained, however, that his primary concern was ensuring such activities took place in an appropriate setting with adult supervision, regardless of gender.

In fact, Anzalone acknowledged that the district has since changed its protocols to ensure administrators are aware of team traditions and that activities such as ice baths have adult supervision. The superintendent also said he wouldn't necessarily have supported ice baths in hotel rooms in the first place, regardless of the athletes' genders.

But the ice bath controversy was hardly the only source of frustration for the girls on the team.

When I asked Anzalone whether he would have handled anything differently, given the protests, the athletes who quit and the turmoil surrounding the program, he acknowledged that the district might have done more to make every student feel supported. He compared the situation to a parent with multiple children, one of whom is going through a particularly difficult time.

"If you have multiple children and one is going through something really serious, you kind of feel like, oh man, am I neglecting the other kids?" Anzalone said. "We want to make sure that we're not doing that. And if we did make those missteps, I know that, at least at the school level, they're working to make sure they correct that."

Anzalone described the situation as a "lose-lose," explaining that supporting one group of students could leave another feeling neglected.

"Trying to find that happy medium," he said, "That's not easy to do."

Anzalone said the controversy has largely quieted down within Camas High School, adding that he hopes students can return to focusing on academics and athletics rather than the political debate surrounding the team.

"It's still from day one, it breaks my heart that any of the students had to kind of take this activist role or decided to take that role," he said.

The superintendent also said he would cooperate fully with the Department of Education's investigation and provide whatever documents federal officials request.

"If there's more that comes out in this, that even I didn't know, then I'll be happy to either answer to it, be accountable to it or change course if necessary," Anzalone said.

The cross-country season may be finished. But for Camas School District, the scrutiny is far from over.

item.title: Locked On Vikings podcaster gets destroyed on social media for anti-Kirk Cousins take
item.description: Luke Braun's viral social media rant against the Kirk Cousins trade to the Vikings drew fierce pushback over his turnover claims and deeper motives.
item.content:encoded:
With the recent trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota, there are a lot of people in the Land of 10,000 Lakes feeling pretty nostalgic these last few days.

After all, Cousins was selected to three Pro Bowls with the Vikings and won them their most recent playoff game.

KIRK COUSINS REVEALS TOUCHING DECISION HIS SONS MADE AFTER TRADE TO VIKINGS: 'LET'S GO!'

Braun took to social media on Tuesday lamenting the move from his beloved Vikings, calling the trade his "long personal nightmare."

"I was always a big Kirk hater when he was here in Minnesota," Braun admits. "Because I thought, hey, this guy is not going to lead us to the promised land."

NFL TRADE DEADLINE WINNERS AND LOSERS, INCLUDING DIANNA RUSSINI AND KIRK COUSINS

The podcaster brought up Cousins' supposed turnover problems and the fact that the Vikings need to protect the ball and stop putting their defense in bad situations.

There's a lot wrong with what Braun said, particularly with the fact that Cousins is statistically one of the safer quarterbacks when it comes to committing turnovers, and the internet saw right through his reasoning.

VIKINGS' CARSON WENTZ WAS HISTORICALLY AWFUL IN LOSS TO BILLS, POSTING A STAT LINE DIFFICULT TO COMPREHEND

Normally, this is the part of the article where I break down everything Braun said that was incorrect, but the fine folks on X stole my thunder and did it for me.

Let's start with Braun's "turnover" claim, which many commenters pointed out is just not true.

Hmmm, okay. So either Braun is misinformed, or there's something deeper to this Kirk Cousins hate that he isn't mentioning.

Of course, the commenters came with receipts for that as well, pointing out that Braun has been a vocal liberal (something that clashes with Cousins' overt Christian family values) and even cited screenshots from his BlueSky account trashing the Wilfs family for the trade and mentioning Michelle Tafoya's political campaign.

So now the truth comes out.

If your reaction to the Vikings going from Kyler Murray to Kirk Cousins is one of disgust, there are probably some deeper, non-football related reasons for it.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

Is Kirk Cousins Joe Montana? No, nor is anyone claiming he is.

But if Cousins can keep up his numbers from the first nine games of the season coupled with Minnesota's defense, the Vikings have a chance to make some noise this postseason.

Don't tell Luke Braun that, though.

item.title: Former owner of Peanut the squirrel, viral pet euthanized by NY officials, detained by ICE
item.description: Nearly two years after New York officials euthanized Peanut the squirrel, his former owners face another ordeal as Daniela Bittner remains in ICE custody.
item.content:encoded:
The wife of the New York man whose viral pet squirrel Peanut was seized and euthanized by wildlife officials in 2024 has been detained by immigration authorities.

Daniela Bittner, a German native, was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in mid-October at a small airport near New York's border with Pennsylvania, according to The Associated Press (AP).

She and her husband of four years, Mark Longo, were planning to attend a TikTok event when officers approached them, according to the New York Post.

Longo said his wife's detention stemmed from what he described as a minor paperwork issue, The AP said. The couple reportedly made an error on one of her immigration forms and failed to catch it while dealing with the seizure and euthanasia of Peanut.

OWNERS OF BELOVED PEANUT THE SQUIRREL PLAN TO SUE NEW YORK STATE OVER SEIZURE AND KILLING BY AUTHORITIES

"She came into this country legally on a visa. We filed the paperwork and stuff and apparently the government is saying we filed the wrong piece of paper," Longo told The Post.

"They had asked for additional information, which we provided, and then apparently they sent a letter stating that it was denied because we filed the wrong paperwork, which we never received," he said.

"This is a minor paperwork issue and it’s being treated as if my wife literally crawled out a hole to get into this country," he added.

PEANUT THE PET SQUIRREL TAKEN AWAY BY NEW YORK STATE OFFICIALS FROM ADOPTED HOME, MAY BE EUTHANIZED

Longo said Bittner has no criminal history and was hit with the maximum penalty, potentially facing deportation without a hearing, according to The Post.

The couple reportedly married in 2022, shortly after Bittner returned to Germany to resolve a visa situation.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) told the outlet that Bittner lawfully entered the U.S. multiple times between May 2021 and November 2022, each time receiving permission to stay for a temporary period.

However, DHS said she was arrested because she "chose to overstay her welcome in defiance of our nation's laws."

"To be clear, a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States," DHS told the Post.

Bittner has reportedly been transferred between several detention centers, from Syracuse to Buffalo, Louisiana and eventually Texas.

Longo described the conditions his wife has faced in federal custody as "deplorable," The AP said.

Her arrest has also cast uncertainty over the couple's nonprofit animal rescue operation, where Bittner reportedly cares for 600 animals rescued from neglect.

"If my wife gets deported for a paperwork issue, we will lose EVERYTHING we worked for. Our Nonprofit Animal Sanctuary will close and 600 animals will have to find another home. All we wanted was to be left alone. We finally moved on from the tragic murder of P'Nut, now to this," he said.

The couple found themselves at the center of a nationwide wildlife controversy in 2024 after New York wildlife officials seized and euthanized their pet squirrel, sparking widespread outrage.

Longo had rescued Peanut when he was just 5 weeks old after the squirrel's mother was reportedly struck and killed by a car. The animal later became a viral social media sensation, amassing a large following online.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Democrat Cindy Holscher wins Kansas governor's race, extending party's hold on governor's mansion
item.description: Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher wins the Kansas governor's race over Trump-backed Republican Ty Masterson, keeping the governor's mansion in Democratic hands.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor’s race, defeating Republican Kansas Senate President Ty Masterson in the open contest to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly, The Associated Press projected.

The victory keeps the governor’s mansion in Democratic hands and marks the third consecutive Kansas gubernatorial election won by a Democrat. Kelly won the office in 2018 and secured a second term in 2022.

The result underscores Democrats’ continued success in Kansas gubernatorial races despite Republicans’ longstanding dominance in the state’s presidential elections. The GOP has carried Kansas in every presidential election since 1968.

GOP WIPEOUT GOES FROM BAD TO WORSE AS DEMS QUIETLY SCORE ANOTHER MAJOR WIN WITH BIG RAMIFICATIONS

Holscher has served in the Kansas Senate since 2021 after previously spending four years in the state House. She secured the Democratic nomination after defeating fellow state Sen. Ethan Corson, who was endorsed by Kelly and former Democratic Gov. Kathleen Sebelius, in the August primary.

Holscher faced scrutiny during the campaign over resurfaced social media posts from 2023 in which she suggested Jesus Christ could have been transgender. The comments came during a debate over proposed Kansas legislation restricting drag performances in front of children.

Holscher celebrated her victory in a post on X, thanking Kansas voters as she prepared to take office.

THE TOP TRUMP OFFICIALS DEMOCRATS ADMIT ARE ON THEIR HIT LIST FOR INVESTIGATIONS IN THE NEW CONGRESS

"Thank you, Kansas! It’s the honor of a lifetime to serve as your next Governor," Holscher wrote.

 Masterson, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump in the crowded GOP primary, conceded the race in a post on X and said he had called Holscher to congratulate her.

"It looks like we will come up just short, but the things we fought for are no less important today than they were yesterday."

Masterson, who has served as Kansas Senate president since 2021, also pointed to Republicans' continued control of the state Legislature and said he would return to the Senate in January to focus on property taxes, public safety, affordability and schools.

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh tees off on Broncos for backing out of trade post deadline: 'Bad precedent'
item.description: Los Angeles Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh blasted the Denver Broncos for using a medical evaluation loophole to renegotiate trade compensation for linebacker Daiyan Henley.
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh called out the Denver Broncos after a trade involving linebacker Daiyan Henley fell through.

The Chargers agreed to trade Henley for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, but Harbaugh said the Broncos wanted to change the 2028 pick compensation based on a pass-fail medical grade.

"The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade, based on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn’t, and we didn’t," Harbaugh told reporters Thursday. "In my opinion, it’s one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent, continues to set a bad precedent."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Broncos were given approval to revisit the terms of the deal with the Chargers after consulting with the NFL on Wednesday, according to The Athletic. The Broncos' medical evaluation of Henley after the trade did not match the Chargers' evaluation before the teams agreed to terms, according to the report.

Harbaugh criticized the Broncos, saying they would have passed Henley on his medical evaluation in exchange for less compensation. He also said the NFL needs to close the loophole.

"Really, it shouldn’t be (a loophole), but apparently it is," Harbaugh said. "That’s why it’s a loophole and teams should not have the ability to do that. I mean, it’s a medical grade. It’s a pass-fail for a medical grade. They told us they weren’t going to pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon, and they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a … fill in the blank. I don’t know what to call that."

The 26-year-old linebacker was on the injury report in Week 9 with a shoulder injury but played 61 of the team's 70 defensive snaps. Harbaugh said he was thrilled to have Henley back.

"He was welcomed back with open arms, and happy about that," Harbaugh said. "What that put Daiyan through, you know, kind of the ringer for the last couple days. Yeah, it’s emotional. It’s painful. And all that’s considered and should be considered by the league when they look into this loophole."

Harbaugh said Henley was back in meetings Thursday. Henley is in his fourth season with the Chargers after being selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Washington State.

In 56 career games, Henley has 317 combined tackles, five sacks, four interceptions and one forced fumble.

item.title: Jared Verse believes a mental block is affecting his play, seeks psychiatrist's help to address it
item.description: Jared Verse reveals he's been meeting with Browns team psychiatrist Mayur Pandya to address the 'mental block' behind his zero sacks this season.
item.content:encoded:
Jared Verse has zero sacks, zero forced fumbles and zero fumble recoveries for the Cleveland Browns this season, and the defensive end believes a mental block could be contributing to his struggles.

Verse, 26, told reporters on Thursday he is working on himself to overcome the frustration he’s feeling over his lack of production. And that work isn’t about lifting more weights, improving his technique or studying his opponents more closely.

"I think it was definitely a mental block," Verse said. "I train my body every day to push myself to the limits of what I’m physically capable of doing. So I don’t think it was any issue with my body, but I think I’ve taken the steps to figure out what it was."

CLEVELAND BROWNS RESET UNDER TODD MONKEN AFTER TRADING MYLES GARRETT AND PARTING WITH STEFANSKI

The steps Verse has taken, he said, include meeting with Browns team psychiatrist Mayur Pandya to address his mental health.

"Obviously, like, I'm upset with the way I've been playing," Verse said. "I don't think it's anything physical. There's nothing wrong with my body. It's not like that. I think it was a mental aspect of the game."

Verse declined to explain exactly how he’s addressing the problem with Pandya but believes he’s close to turning a corner as a result.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I think I've attacked it very well these last couple weeks, but I think this past week is a big key thing that I've done is I'm very excited for this next week," Verse said.

"I took a lot of time for self-growth. I met with Dr. Pandya a little bit, and I figured out what my issue was."

Times have truly changed in American society.

The Greatest Generation went to war, defeated the Nazis of Germany and the imperialists of Japan and stamped the United States as the strongest country on the planet, all at a great cost to their mental and physical health, but seemingly never complained about it.

But athletes today struggle with contracts, or statistics, or their home lives, and do not hesitate to have their mental health checked.

That could be seen as progress.

But it could also be seen in some sectors — particularly in the high-octane NFL — as weakness.

Verse seemed to touch on that by suggesting there are limits to what is acceptable as individuals address their mental health.

"You can't go out there and start doing some crazy things like going to, like, I'm training with a monk or something that," he said.

But, clearly, professional mental help is something Verse believes is about to help him change the narrative of his 2026 season.

"I think the Browns fans are upset about it, I'm upset about it, I think we all have a reason to be upset," he said. "I just haven't done enough, and I think I'll take any time to figure out what the issue was. I've attacked it. I think I'm ready for this week."

item.title: Teachers union spent nearly $8M to crush school choice, biological sports measures, report finds
item.description: Defending Education uncovered how the NEA and affiliates spent nearly $7.8 million fighting ballot measures and school choice campaigns in three states.
item.content:encoded:
The country's largest teachers union and its affiliates poured nearly $7.8 million into ballot fights across three states in 2026, as internal documents outlined strategies to target voucher programs and other conservative initiatives, according to Defending Education (DE).

In a recent report, the education watchdog uncovered a guidance document from the National Education Association (NEA) which stated that "unions may spend unlimited amounts from their general treasuries on ballot measures in any state, subject to any state affiliate agreements to address specific state laws." Additionally, DE found that the NEA calls for providing "strategic and financial assistance" to defeat unfriendly ballot measures.

DE senior director of communications Erika Sanzi, a former teacher and NEA member, told Fox News Digital that the union has shifted towards politics over the years. She said that instead of talking about education, the union has become focused on issues like the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, climate change and gender ideology, among others.

"I 100% believe that the union has done a lot of damage and continues to do a lot damage," Sanzi told Fox News Digital. "I also think that they've become much more political and much more ideological than they used to be."

UNEARTHED FILING SHOWS LARGEST TEACHERS UNIONS POURED OVER $900 MILLION INTO POLITICAL ACTIVITIES

The financial findings in DE's report show the union's spending on political fights across the country.

On Sept. 30, 2026, the Arizona Education Association sent $75,000 to Will of The People PAC, a group that opposed Proposition 318, according to DE. The proposition was approved and will require all schools and athletic associations to restrict access to private spaces and sports participation based on biological sex.

The Washington state NEA affiliate Washington Education Association contributed more than $391,000 to No Hate in WA State, DE found. The group opposed two ballot measures, one of which was aimed at restoring parents' rights in public schools. The other ballot measure, which was approved, will require sex verification for participation in women's sports.

In Alaska, the NEA Advocacy Fund contributed $250,000 to the group "No on 2," which opposed Alaska's Ballot Measure No. 2, which sought to repeal the state's top-four ranked-choice voting system.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

The grassroots group found that in the first two quarters of 2026, the Protect Education, Accountability Now PAC received $7,075,438.33 from the Arizona Education Association and the NEA for an anti-school choice campaign. DE said in its report that "the PAC appears to be run and operated by the president of an NEA local affiliate – Kyrene Education Association."

Fox News Digital was unable to independently confirm whether the PAC and the Kyrene Education Association share leadership.

Beyond the contributions detailed in the report, the NEA has made its opposition to voucher programs, arguing that they take away resources from public schools and have racist origins. A Feb. 13, 2026, post on NEA Today, the union's blog, claimed that "voucher expansion is re-segregating schools by race and income and reflects a policy rooted in resistance to school integration."

However, Sanzi told Fox News Digital that there is a fundamental misunderstanding of what school choice actually means.

"What I try to remind people of is school choice doesn't mean that the public school won't be the choice," Sanzi told Fox News Digital. "For the majority of families, the local public school is the choice, it just means that they have other options and alternatives as well."

DENVER MOTHER FIGHTS FOR HER DAUGHTER'S EDUCATION AS ADVOCATES MAKE NATIONWIDE SCHOOL CHOICE PUSH

DE’s report also examines the NEA’s efforts to preserve dues revenue as states restrict payroll deductions.

In 2025, the NEA released a document titled "AutoPay Playbook," which was obtained by DE. The playbook lays out the union's objections to payroll deduction bans, which the union argued were intended "to force affiliates into all-consuming conversion campaigns that prevent our union from building the power we need to protect public education."

The NEA’s playbook describes proactively moving members to AutoPay as "the only way to neutralize this threat and protect our power" in the face of payroll deduction bans. The union warns that fast-moving state legislation can leave affiliates with "near-impossible timelines" to make the switch.

The AutoPay program, according to DE, relies on recurring electronic funds transfers to collect membership dues.

"The idea that they wanna compel people into this AutoPay system, it's in part because it gives all the power to the union versus the school district and the member," Sanzi told Fox News Digital. She added that members could "get stuck" in a subscription model, where payments are continuous and often forgotten about.

Sanzi noted that parents often conflate supporting their children’s teachers with supporting union leadership.

"I think people feel obligated to be in favor of the teacher's union because they hear the word teachers, and they want to be supportive of their children's teachers. But the union and the rank and file teachers are two very different entities," she told Fox News Digital.

The NEA did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Dianna Russini's cringe podcast debut raises questions about the viability of her comeback
item.description: Dianna Russini's BetUS TV debut crashed the site but dodged the Mike Vrabel scandal, joking about memes instead of addressing accountability.
item.content:encoded:
Dianna Russini debuted her new project with offshore gambling company BetUS on Wednesday. Again, Russini avoided addressing the Mike Vrabel scandal or taking any accountability.

She did, however, joke about memes related to the scandal.

"I’ve seen all the memes and comments … and some of you guys are really funny," Russini said on the "Russin Report."

She referenced a viral AI video showing her playing the saxophone alongside Vrabel. Russini said that if she played an instrument, it would be the saxophone. Later, she credited AI with making her look like an "L.A. 10."

If there was one bright spot in the debut, it was that Russini didn't plead for sympathy, as she did earlier in the week in an interview with People.

DIANNA RUSSINI IS PLANNING A RETURN TO UNKNOWN SPORTS MEDIA POSITION 'NEXT WEEK' AFTER SCANDAL

During that discussion, she claimed she was the victim of "heartbreaking lies" and said she wanted to be an inspiration to other women.

Russini did not specify which claims about her were "lies."

Considering there is photographic evidence of her and Vrabel together dating back seven years, it is hard to dispute that she failed to disclose a personal relationship, romantic or otherwise, with someone she covered and used as a source. That undisclosed relationship was the reason The Athletic gave for finding her in violation of company standards.

Judging by the reaction from various members of the media, Russini did little this week to improve perceptions of her. She continues to handle this poorly, as if she truly believes she did nothing wrong.

That is why the outlook for her new project could be dim.

BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL

Unsurprisingly, her first episode drew substantial interest. The website hosting the show, BetUS TV, crashed because of the traffic. The reason for that interest was obvious: People wanted to see whether she would address the scandal. Because she didn't, that interest is unlikely to carry over to future episodes.

Can Russini generate enough interest by discussing football? Given concerns about her credibility and criticism of her lack of accountability, that could be difficult.

Entertaining an audience requires different skills than breaking NFL news. Most successful hosts build a connection with their audience through trust and authenticity.

That will be a hard sell for Dianna Russini.

She has become increasingly unlikable and cringeworthy since the scandal began. She talks down to her audience as if she expects everyone to accept that she was simply a victim.

She wasn't. And no honest person could think she was.

Let us know: Do you have any interest in watching Russini host a weekly podcast?

item.title: Mamdani prepares to fulfill promise to axe NYPD unit responsible for controlling protest violence
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is reportedly preparing to disband the NYPD's Strategic Response Group after months of failing to fulfill his promise to do so.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is reportedly preparing to announce his plan to disband the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), fulfilling a long-held campaign promise that has led to mounting pressure from his base, as well as questions about how the group's duties will be replaced.

Politico reported that Mamdani, a democratic socialist, is preparing to announce plans to disband the unit, which responds to protests, civil disturbances and major events while handling counterterrorism operations.

Mamdani has said he wants to decouple the unit’s protest and counterterrorism functions, but at a March City Council budget hearing Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said discussions with the mayor concerned "the future of how we police protests generally," not disbanding the unit.

MAMDANI IN HOT SEAT OVER POST MOURNING DEATH OF INMATE CHARGED WITH CALLOUS CRIME: 'ABSOLUTELTY SHAMEFUL'

The NYPD says the SRG responds to citywide mobilizations, civil disorders and major events and is a "critical asset" during parades, protests and the papal visit. SRG personnel are "also deployed to areas requiring an increased police presence due to increased crime or other conditions" and "mobilizes for shootings, bank robberies, missing persons, demonstrations, or other significant incidents," according to the department.

Tisch added during the March City Council budget hearing that the SRG does not typically deal with peaceful protests, but is deployed for protests that involve criminal activity. She also noted that in 2025 the NYPD facilitated 4,255 protests and the SRG was available at 245 of them, or roughly 6%.

Sources familiar with the plan told Politico that City Hall has been contemplating putting the SRG under Mamdani's new Office of Community Safety, launched earlier this year. The sources also said Mamdani's plan could be formalized via an executive order, according to Politico.

MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS

"I've been clear that my vision is for the disbanding of the SRG. And the reason for that vision is that the SRG were created a little more than a decade ago with an intention first of dealing with threats, terroristic threats to the city," Mamdani said during a press conference in September.

"What it has eventually become is both dealing with counterterrorism and responses to exercising First Amendment rights," the mayor continued. "I do not believe that those purposes need to be dual purposes. I believe that we should have a focus on counterterrorism that is separate from our response to the use of First Amendment — [that] continues to be a conversation I'm having with our police commissioner."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Fox News Digital reached out to City Hall for confirmation and comment on the mayor's reported plan, but did not hear back in time for publication.

"As the Mayor has said, our administration will disband the Strategic Response Group and separate protest response from counterterrorism," spokesperson Dora Pekec told Politico. "We will have more to share soon."

Fox News Digital reached out to the NYPD for comment.
