item.title: Chick-fil-A customers have days left to order cult favorite sandwich before it vanishes
item.description: Chicken & Waffles exit most Chick-fil-A menus on Nov. 14, but Tampa, Chicago and Raleigh diners can still order expanded waffle breakfast options.
item.content:encoded:
Chick-fil-A is pulling a seasonal favorite from its menus, but some lucky diners in certain cities may still have a chance to order it.

The chain's Chicken & Waffles sandwiches are leaving most menus on Nov. 14, or while supplies last, but select restaurants in Tampa, Chicago and Raleigh will keep serving a breakfast version as the chain tests four additional waffle sandwiches.

The nationwide limited-time offering debuted in August after a test run in 2025, pairing the chain's chicken filet with maple-flavored waffles, applewood smoked bacon, honey butter spread and syrup.

MCDONALD'S MCRIB RETURNS FOR LIMITED TIME, BUT CUSTOMERS IN SOME CITIES WILL MISS OUT

"We've loved seeing how much our guests enjoyed Chicken & Waffles this fall, especially the breakfast sandwich," Allison Duncan, Chick-fil-A's director of menu and packaging, told QSR.

But beginning Nov. 16, participating restaurants in the three cities will offer the Chicken & Waffles Breakfast Sandwich with an Original, Spicy or Grilled filet, along with Chicken, Egg & Cheese; Bacon, Egg & Cheese; Sausage, Egg & Cheese; and Grilled Chicken, Bacon, Egg & Cheese waffle sandwiches. The test menu will be available during breakfast hours, until 10:30 a.m.

POPEYES BRINGS BACK POPULAR MENU ITEM FOR GOOD, AND NOT EVERYONE IS HAPPY

Chick-fil-A selects test markets based on opportunities to gather feedback from customers and local owner-operators, the company told Fox News Digital. The company did not identify participating restaurants but said individual locations typically share test menu details on their social media pages.

Customers in the test cities can also check the Chick-fil-A app to see whether their local restaurant is participating.

CHICK-FIL-A'S FIRST NEW SAUCE IN 10 YEARS HAS FANS SHARING STRONG REACTION

Duncan said the company hopes the test will help it learn what customers want next. Chick-fil-A has not announced whether the expanded menu could come to more locations.

Online, fans are mourning the nationwide exit.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

In a Reddit post about the exit, one person said, "I wish it would stay. I ordered it every time."

Another commenter called it "the only [limited-time offer] I've ever really liked." It was "the best breakfast sandwich in the game," the person said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

But others don't mind seeing the item go. Some Reddit users said the waffles were too dense or not soft enough to soak up the syrup, while others said they were excited that the limited-time item was making room for something new.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The chicken and waffles were part of a yearlong "Newstalgia"-inspired celebration, which the company said offered "a delicious twist on familiar favorites." Along with it came a s'mores milkshake and frosted coffee lineup, which are also ending on Nov. 14.

The menu change comes as Chick-fil-A's holiday lineup arrives Nov. 16. It includes a new Peppermint Cream Cold Brew, returning peppermint drinks and Chicken Tortilla Soup, along with Spicy Chick-fil-A Sauce, which is joining the nationwide menu permanently, Fox News Digital reported last month.

item.title: Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor forced to retire as health battle threatens hearing
item.description: Roger Taylor says his tinnitus has been "getting steadily worse," forcing the iconic Duran Duran drummer to step away after decades on stage.
item.content:encoded:
Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor announced he is "retiring from playing the drums" and stepping away from the band due to health concerns.

The band released a statement on their official Instagram, noting his retirement comes on the heels of "a worsening of his recently diagnosed tinnitus."

"This is one of the hardest decisions I’ve ever had to make," Taylor said in the statement. "Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I’ll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they’ve shown us over the years. But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse, and I’ve reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors."

He went on to say that "figuring out the timing of all of this has not been easy, but I’m going out on a real high."

THE OFFSPRING GUITARIST KEVIN ‘NOODLES’ WASSERMAN STEPS AWAY FROM TOURING OVER ‘SERIOUS HEALTH ISSUE’

He noted that the band "just returned from a hugely successful UK and European tour," after which they headlined a show at BST Hyde Park for the second time, returned to record in the studio with guitarist Nile Rodgers and were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

"I couldn’t have asked for a better final chapter, with so many special moments that I’ll treasure forever," he added. "I move on with enormous pride, and with nothing but love for Simon, Nick and John."

The statement highlighted Taylor's contributions to the band's success, noting he "has been at the heart of Duran Duran’s sound across two remarkable chapters," first in its "era-defining early records" and then again when the original line-up reunited in 2001.

After coming back together in 2001, the group released six more chart-topping albums, with Taylor "performing with them to millions of fans around the world."

"After careful consideration and medical advice, he has decided that protecting his hearing and long-term health must now come first," the statement read.

Fellow band members Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes and John Taylor also shared their thoughts, calling Taylor "our brother," and crediting his drumming for helping "define the sound of Duran Duran from the very beginning."

"Having him back with us since 2001 has been incredibly important to us all," they said. "We completely support his decision and wish him health and happiness. He will always be part of this family, while we continue exploring new and exciting projects with the band."

The post was accompanied by photos of Taylor on stage performing with the band.

Fans of the band took to the comments section to wish the musician well as he closes this chapter of his life. One of them was his son, Elliot, who wrote, "Not a bad run, Dad! 🤘 loved capturing some of these moments on stage with you 📸 ❤️."

"Your rhythm has been the soundtrack to the best moments of my life and entire generations," another added. "Even though you are choosing silence now to take care of yourself, your beat will echo forever in our lives. Thank you for everything Roger!❤️🥁"

Duran Duran formed in the late 1970s, releasing their self-titled debut album in 1981 and quickly making a name for themselves as a group ready to push the boundaries. They became household names with the release of their second album, "Rio," in 1982, which featured hits such as "Hungry Like the Wolf."

Despite their success, the band split in the mid-1980s, with two members, including Taylor, pursuing solo projects. However, they came back together in 2001 and released an album with all five original members from the '80s in 2004.

"I think there was always a sense of unfinished business with the original five," Taylor told The Chronicle in 2022. "I think that was a feeling that there was definitely more gas in the tank when we broke up. I think we all felt that, and we came back together and it was pretty amazing."

As a band, they have won two Grammy Awards, have a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022.

item.title: NFL great Barry Sanders taps beer keg in Munich, battles through the adversity of a poorly designed mallet
item.description: Barry Sanders donned a protective apron to tap a beer keg Oktoberfest-style in Munich before the Detroit Lions took on the New England Patriots.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is continuing with its European slate (which I enjoy; how are people mad at a Sunday morning coffee and football-watching sesh?) in Munich, with the Detroit Lions taking on the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena.

And what better way to get people fired up than by letting an all-time great take a turn at tapping a beer keg Oktoberfest-style?

...Right, there isn't one, and that's why Lions legend Barry Sanders threw on a protective apron to show us how it's done.

NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT'

Turns out this is way harder than it looks.

Not a bad first attempt by the Hall of Famer, but poor Barry was just thrown to, as the Germans would say, "der wolves."

First of all, do they not have normal mallets? I've never been to Germany (though I do have an affinity for bratwursts and the music of Kraftwerk), so maybe they don't.

I don't want to tell the Germans how to tap a keg, but wouldn't that be way easier with a flat-sided rubber mallet? They're using the mallet that someone stole from a Whac-A-Mole machine at the arcade down the Straße.

Get Barry a real American mallet, and that keg would be tapped so hard the Germans would be more in awe of him than they are of David Hasselhoff.

And there was no help from that mascot.

That wasn't the normal Lions mascot, Roary; that was their German mascot, Leo Löwe.

Leo, mein Freund, when you see your franchise's greatest legend struggling to tap a keg, maybe lend a paw. Don't just lean on the keg like you're trying to be the Arthur Fonzarelli of the keg party.

I'm not mad, just disappointed.

But all that matters is that Barry got the job done, despite all that was working against him.

And man, imagine the stories those Lions fans have.

"I drank beer from a keg tapped by Barry Sanders... after several tries, but it was because they gave him a bum mallet."
